name: DISPUTE_TERMS
rule: 2: magic, version = 2, exact length 136, reserved zero, the two windows nonzero and at or below revision 7's 2^62, executor_reward_bps <= 10000, bond_slasher_bps <= 10000, bond_policy_kind != 0, kind/field agreement, bond_remainder != 0 under either kind, under kind = 2 a bond that is 0 or >= 890,880, and abandon_after_slots >= 1.  **2c', the per-template comparison, checks 17-20:** min_abandon_after_slots <= abandon_after_slots <= max_abandon_after_slots, challenge_window_slots <= max_challenge_window_slots, response_window_slots <= max_response_window_slots, and abandon_after_slots <= max_document_lifetime_slots -- all five read from the template's own DTU1, which is why the four protocol-wide caps of round 3 and round 4 are WITHDRAWN and DCG enforces nothing else about a document's windows
positive_vector: the example terms decode, and the same terms pass 17-20 under the example template
negative_vector: kind = 0; bps = 10001; bond_remainder = 0; a bond of 1 under kind 2; an abandonment window of 0; and at 2c' a grace one under the template's floor (2,591,999 against 2,592,000), a grace over its ceiling, a challenge window of 67,108,865 against the example template's 67,108,864, a response window of 8,388,609, and the same 5,184,000 grace under the SHORT-lived template whose ceiling is 4,096,000

name: RUN_BINDING
rule: DRB1 v2 decodes; executor = the signer; first = prompt_positions - 1; the output locator equals PT2S 426/430/431; completion: first + count + 1 <= position_capacity; decision: first + 1 <= position_capacity; decision count = 1 + option_count; output_width = 16 when stop_plus_one != 0; decision_flags bit 0 <=> option_count != 0; output_width = 4 when that bit is set; the option-table hash; and 1 <= option_count <= 80 for form 47; and, when option_count != 0, every write output_write + i for i in 1..=option_count exists at output_first_position with width 4, and output_write + option_count <= 255
positive_vector: the example binding decodes and binds
negative_vector: option_count = 81; first != prompt_positions - 1; a moved locator; a 17-byte width; a missing per-cell write; a u8 write overflow

name: PLAN_BINDING
instruction: every handler that reads the template
rule: DCM2 v7, a DCR2 v6, a PT2S whose base accounts bind, and a /5 descriptor at the PDAs
negative_vector: a DCM2 v6 account (780/580 at a plain record read, 785 where a plan binds)

name: OUTPUT_PROOF
rule: index < L; the bit is clear; the position's root is landed; flag 2 is set; the leaf's write row matches (write output_write + i at output_first_position under decision_flags bit 0); the SPP1 folds to the root
negative_vector: index = L (591 at the index test), or any index before finalize

name: RESULT_STATE
rule: the record is PENDING and open; outputs_attested = L; for a completion the stop rule over outputs [0, L).  On revision 8 the close runs this SAME check before it closes when flag 4 is clear, so a stop-rule convict cannot attest its last output and close in one transaction (round-3 High 3): met => SETTLED, violated => flag 4, challenger_wins + 1, REFUTED, and the policy with cause 4
positive_vector: a document with outputs_attested = L whose stop rule passes
negative_vector: outputs_attested != L, or a stop-rule violation

name: CL_AUTHORITY
rule: the close and the settle each take 9 metas under either kind, and the kind is read from the terms: under kind = 1 the winner meta equals the recorded winner (or the incinerator when it is zero) and the remainder meta equals terms.bond_remainder; under kind = 2 the escrow meta equals the derived bond escrow and there is no destination meta; the executor meta equals DCM2 40; tag 186's recipient is DTU1's authority; a tag 186 pays each resource's recorded payer
positive_vector: the example STANDARD close with 9 metas
negative_vector: 8 or 10 metas under either kind; a substituted winner; a STANDARD list on a CUSTOM document

name: CL_MISSING
rule: flag 2 is set before any output is attested; positions_complete = n at finalize.  A finalized, unrefuted document closes on row 1 when outputs_attested = L and on row 3 when it is below L, so 796 is NOT a close refusal on revision 8: the withheld-attestation row is the exit, and it waits for the LATER of the two deadlines

name: CL_CLOSE
rule: at 172: NO close row matched -- a finalized document with now <= dispute_deadline or open_challenges != 0; an unfinalized one with now < abandon_deadline; a finalized, flag-4-clear one with outputs_attested < L and either now <= dispute_deadline or now < abandon_deadline (row 3's own window test, so a withheld document waits for the LATER of the two deadlines).  This is revision 7's own 'not closeable yet' code.  At 187: the escrow exists, is the document's escrow and holds lamports; the result is a closed DCR2 v6 with bond_state = 4, or a DCRZ v2 with bond_escrowed = 1 (the status byte is NOT tested -- a conviction close leaves REFUTED and a withheld one WITHHELD, and both are live); the document is CUSTOM (settlement_program != 0)
positive_vector: a retry on a document whose program has been fixed, before or after retention
negative_vector: an early close on any of the three rows; a second retry; a retry with no escrow; a retry on a STANDARD document; a retry after the settle cleared bond_state

name: the overflow code revision 7 already owns
rule: every deadline add is a CHECKED add in u64 and none of them is saturating or wrapping: init_slot + challenge_window_slots and init_slot + abandon_after_slots at 161, slot + abandon_after_slots at 162 and 165, and revision 7's own now + retention_slots and the drain at 172.  Round 4 removed 177 from this row: AttestOutputV5 no longer writes abandon_deadline at all, so it has no add.  With the template's own limits (DTU1 88) the three window terms are bounded by 2^27, so none of these can overflow at a reachable slot; the check is stated anyway because a wrapping_add would pass every vector in this file and be wrong
positive_vector: the example's three adds, all far from 2^64
negative_vector: a terms block whose window plus a slot near 2^64 would wrap (unreachable once the caps are in force, and refused 791 before it could be written)

name: SETTLEMENT_PROGRAM
rule: the program meta equals terms.settlement_program and is executable; after the CPI the escrow is 0, no other account lost lamports, and the result account's only change is bond_state -> 0
negative_vector: a callee that keeps a lamport (D12's named non-case); a closed program

name: DEADLINE (revision 7's reused code)
rule: TWO rules, both at 165, both this code. (i) now < abandon_deadline: a document that has sat past its own production window is no longer producible, and it is closable on row 2 by anyone with its rent and bond returned, so the refusal costs the executor nothing -- and it is what makes finalize_slot <= init_slot + the template's max_document_lifetime_slots a bound rather than a hope. (ii) now <= init_slot + DTU1[104] - abandon_after_slots, where DTU1[104] is THE TEMPLATE'S max_document_lifetime_slots: a finalize that would leave less than one full attestation budget is refused, with init_slot := DCM2[144] - DCM2[184] and every value read BEFORE finalize's own write. Check 20 (abandon_after_slots <= the template's lifetime limit) is what keeps that subtraction total, and it is checked. Rule (ii) is a decision, not tooling guidance: allowing the late finalize convicts an honest executor WITHHELD and takes the whole pot under a STANDARD policy, while the refusal leaves the document closable on row 2 with cause 0. With (ii) in force the clamp can never bind at finalize, so the deadline finalize writes is always finalize_slot + abandon_after_slots
positive_vector: a finalize one slot before abandon_deadline, inside the budget: the deadline it writes is finalize_slot + abandon_after_slots, and the clamp does not bind
negative_vector: now >= abandon_deadline (i); now > init_slot + THE TEMPLATE'S max_document_lifetime_slots - abandon_after_slots, which at abandon_after_slots == max_abandon_after_slots == that limit means any finalize after the document's own init slot (ii); a finalize whose 144 has already been rewritten, which the 592 on flag 2 refuses first

name: DOCUMENT_LENGTH
rule: option_count = 0: 1 <= n <= position_capacity and first + 2 <= n <= first + count + 1; option_count != 0: n = prompt_positions, first = n - 1 and count = 1 + option_count
positive_vector: the example finalize at n = 500, F = 16
negative_vector: n = first + 1; n = first + count + 2; count = 1 on a decision

name: DECISION_OPTION_FORM
rule: revision 8 refuses option_count == 0 or option_count > 80 for the single-reducer form; revision 7 retains its historical code 816

name: TEMPLATE_USED
rule: tag 186 requires state in {0,1,2} and documents = 0; init requires state == 0
positive_vector: a single-base template with no live documents
negative_vector: a live document or a malformed/closed template record

name: TEMPLATE_SEAL
instruction: the template seal, UnifiedInit 2b and 2c, LandPositionRoots, FinalizeDocumentV5
rule: the seal's own bounds on the five limits it writes into DTU1: every limit nonzero, min_abandon_after_slots <= max_abandon_after_slots, max_abandon_after_slots <= max_document_lifetime_slots, and limit + seal_slot representable -- **no magnitude, because DCG sets no default durations**.  The same code answers a structurally wrong DTU1 at any reader: wrong magic, wrong version, wrong length, a nonzero reserved run, the wrong PDA, or an inconsistent set of limits.  At tags 162 and 165 `state` is deliberately NOT read, so a document under a retired template can still land and finalize
positive_vector: a template sealed with the example template's five limits, and the same DTU1 read by a landing, a finalize and an init
negative_vector: a zero limit; a floor above its ceiling; a grace maximum above the lifetime; a limit that would overflow against the seal's slot; a DTU1 at another address, or one of 87 bytes

name: PT1O_RESERVATION_REQUIRED
rule: a request whose exact PT1O size exceeds 10,240 bytes requires the binding-derived PDA to be fully reserved at that exact size; a fresh PDA, partial PT1R reservation, oversized reservation or PT1O with a mismatched stream length returns this code before output bytes are written
positive_vector: tag 199 completed the bounded reserve steps; or a prior PT1O has matching binding, length and PT1P metadata
negative_vector: tag 146 without reserve; an incomplete or oversized PT1R reservation; PT1O with the wrong stream length; wrong magic or binding (InvalidAccountData)

name: CL_MALFORMED, the structural refusal at the call site's own code
rule: a revision-7 record is not reinterpreted: DCM2 v6, DCR2 v5, DDT2 v1, DRB1 v1, DCRZ v1-as-read-by-a-rev-8-close and a /4 descriptor all refuse on a version field, never on a zero-byte convention; the code is the one the call site already uses, 580 for a record read as a record, 785 where a plan binds, 791 for a DDT2 block, 794 for a DRB1 block

name: INVALID_INSTRUCTION_DATA
rule: ProgramError::InvalidInstructionData (the existing builtin code 2) is returned before handler dispatch when instruction data is empty or its leading tag is outside the explicit revision-8 surface; tags 131/132 route only through unified DCR1 and cannot fall through to standalone root-only handlers
positive_vector: any listed revision-8 tag reaches its typed route, including 131/132 with a revision-8 unified DCR1
negative_vector: an empty instruction, any unlisted tag, or a standalone root-only 131/132 call
